title: Derived pullback preserves perfect complexes
statement: Let g:T\to X be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let E be a perfect object of D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex]. The derived pullback Lg^*E [def-pc-derived-pullback] is perfect on T.

proof.text: For t in T, unfold IsPerfect and take the supplied neighbourhood U of g(t), strictly perfect complex K, and isomorphism E restricted to U with Q(K). Use V = g inverse-image U as the neighbourhood of t.

Construct localizedPullback g U. The open-site unit isomorphisms and pullbackObjUnitToUnit give its unit isomorphism; the latter is invertible because inverse image of opens preserves the terminal open, hence is final. As a left adjoint the functor preserves coproducts, so sigmaComparison and Sigma.mapIso identify its finite free images. Apply the functor to each finite-free retract and compose with this isomorphism; functoriality preserves the splitting equation. Additivity maps the zero terms to zero, preserving the original bounds. Thus the termwise pulled complex is strictly perfect.

Apply localizedPullback_perfectModel_iso to the given local model isomorphism. Combine its derived-object identification with the strictly perfectness just proved and the membership t in V. These are exactly the witnesses of IsPerfect at t.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09UA, alternative local-model proof via 09U7; Q1 explicitly proved finite-free and retract preservation and the localized computation.
